hypothesis: Holding still before the first enemy shot removes the moving-target transition that caused early received hits and shield aborts in v436. The first qualifying strong shot should already target a stationary anchor and be available for an immediate sidestep/intercept attempt.

prior_evidence.interpretation: Several rounds shielded32..36shots without aborting, while early transition rounds reached3received hits after few shield collisions. This motivates an opening-only change; it does not establish a probability of success.

changes: In battles that began as pure duels, hold position from tick0 and orient the body perpendicular to the first available scanned enemy position while waiting for the first true shot; release after35ticks if no shot is observed.
Track the actual stationarySince timestamp before shield activation, including the entire opening hold.

Classify the earliest true observed shot using a production openingDecision method. Activate on a finite power at least2.4, shot and current range at least275, own energy above35, shot age0..4, and at least3 stationary ticks before the shot.
On strong-shot activation, continue into the existing true-wave candidate handler in the same tick, allowing that first stationary-target shot to initiate the sidestep.

On a weak, short, otherwise ineligible first shot or timeout, return to normal movement and release normal gun firing on the following local tick. Preserve later true-wave eligibility; releasing the opening does not disable future shielding.
Suppress initial normal real shots while retaining gun data manager execution, virtual gun evaluation, normal aim updates, movement state tracking, and radar updates.
Add opening_ticks, activation_time, and first_received_time to the existing once-per-round TITAN_SHIELD diagnostic.

Retain the v436 side step, actual intercept solver, minimum60pixel intercept bound, phase selection, next-tick fire checks, projectile tracking, endgame exit, and three-hit abort. Retain v435 round-owner fix and memory format.
